author: Allen Huang,Frederik Anseel
description:
On July 13, more than 200 leading economists and AI researchers, including 16 Nobel laureates, signed an open letter organised by the Stanford Digital Economy Lab. Its warning was stark: artificial intelligence may drive an economic transformation “larger than the Industrial Revolution” compressed into a fraction of the time, and that we “must act now” to build the institutions to steer it.
We agree with every word. Then we scanned the signatory list. Four in five signatories come from the...
title: The West is debating AI’s future with half the world absent

author: Yuanyue Dang
description:
One morning in February 1784, a converted privateer called the Empress of China sailed out of New York harbour. It was bound for a country almost no one aboard had ever seen – China, then ruled by the Qing dynasty.
Six months later, it dropped anchor at Canton, the only port where the Qing government allowed Western maritime trade.
At the time, the Declaration of Independence was less than a decade old, and the Treaty of Paris recognising American independence had been signed less than a year...
title: How America’s 250-year China dream became its greatest strategic challenge

author: Alice Li
description:
China finished the first high-speed railway tunnel under the Yangtze River on Friday, marking a major step forward in the construction of a line that will one day connect the inland of the country with the coast.
The 11.9km (7.4-mile) Caiyuanba Yangtze River Railway Tunnel links two districts in Chongqing and will be a key link in a high-speed line between two key hubs in the southwestern megacity and Xiamen in the southeastern province of Fujian.
The project had to overcome the challenges posed...
title: China completes first high-speed rail tunnel under the Yangtze River

author: Jevans Nyabiage
description:
Beijing’s soft power drive to win African hearts through cinema was on display recently in Bujumbura, where Chinese dragon and lion dances merged with sacred Burundian drums to open Chinese Film Week.
The Chinese embassy in Bujumbura, the economic capital of Burundi, said the July 15 event offered “a beautiful example of cultural exchanges between the two countries” and that both sides were determined to “make cinema a vehicle for Sino-Burundian friendship”.
Zhu Kewei, China’s ambassador to the...
title: How China is using film diplomacy to project a better image across Africa

author: Lawrence Chung
description:
A People’s Liberation Army helicopter’s unprecedented flight in the Taiwan Strait has raised concerns in Taipei that Beijing is rehearsing a new kind of operation for a potential cross-strait conflict.
Taiwan’s defence ministry said it detected four PLA aircraft, including a helicopter and an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV), operating around the island on July 20 and the following morning.
The helicopter and drone crossed the median line and remained east of it for nearly 9.5 hours in the “R9”...
title: What a helicopter’s flight in the Taiwan Strait says about Beijing’s war plans

author: Phoebe Zhang
description:
Trains were stopped, schools were halted and residents were evacuated in southern China as Typhoon Noul headed towards the coast.
The National Meteorological Centre issued an orange typhoon alert – the second highest level in a four-tier system – on Saturday morning as it moved northwest across the South China Sea at a speed of 20km/h (12mph).
It was expected to land somewhere between Hong Kong and Huilai county in eastern Guangdong overnight with wind speeds of up to 151km/h and then move...
title: Shenzhen rail and air services cancelled as southern China braces for Typhoon Noul

author: Caroline Lin
description:
Chinese defence suppliers are hitting a wall when it comes to translating national strategic goals into effective enterprise-level actions, according to an analysis by industry insiders.
The study, published in May by the academic journal Defence Industry Conversion in China, identified four major challenges that might undermine the implementation of Beijing’s 2026-2030 plan for the national defence industry.
Authors Gao Xufeng and Wu Ke are strategic planning researchers from the Chengdu-based...
title: Can China’s aerospace industry overcome ‘execution gap’ in modernisation goals?

author: Shi Huang
description:
In 138BC, Chinese diplomat and explorer Zhang Qian was sent as an envoy to the western regions.
The Han dynasty envoy failed to achieve his emperor’s goal of launching a pincer attack against the Xiongnu nomadic confederation, but he unexpectedly discovered a route.
The land route started from Changan, present-day Xian, and passed through Gansu province and the Xinjiang Uygur autonomous region, reaching Central and West Asia, and connecting various countries along the Mediterranean.

title: Long before the Silk Road, silkworm cocoons already existed in Uzbekistan
